name: cycle_frame_counter_and_offset
description: Advances a four-step cycle counter in a per-object record while a flag is set, calling one routine to reset the timing when the cycle restarts. It then writes a computed value into a field whose offset depends on a secondary mode flag.

name: install_conditional_jump_redirect
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer stored in an object, then branches on the returned status word and writes a jump-instruction opcode and a target address into a global location. The tail of the routine is decompiler bad data, so only this setup part is recoverable.

name: call_three_subroutines
description: Six-instruction routine that is referenced by address and calls three other routines, one of which it reaches through a pointer. No pseudo-code was produced, so its body beyond this call structure is not recoverable.

name: forward_single_call_stub
description: Four-instruction routine that is referenced by address and forwards control to one other routine, and is reached from one caller. No pseudo-code was produced, so nothing beyond this call relationship is known.

name: merge_constant_then_call
description: Eleven-instruction routine that merges a constant into the data register and then calls three other routines. It is referenced by address from a single caller, and no pseudo-code was produced.

name: forward_to_routine_call
description: Three-instruction routine that is referenced by address, reached from two callers, and calls one other routine. No pseudo-code was produced, so its behaviour is limited to that call structure.

name: clear_selected_bit_across_planes
description: Clears one bit, chosen from the low bits of a data register, in bytes at fixed offsets from two base pointers, and then zeroes a byte at a third pointer. The leading toggle pair cancels out, and the trailing decompiler bad-data note is not behaviour.

name: set_word_bits_then_clear
description: Sets the two high-order bits of a 16-bit word at an offset computed from a data register, then clears one bit selected by the low bits of that register in several byte locations. It finishes by zeroing a byte at an output pointer.

name: invoke_shared_vector_slot
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer at a fixed offset in a shared global block, then returns the value the data register D1 holds afterwards. It is reached from five callers.

name: forward_boot_entry_call
description: Single-instruction boot block entry that the Kickstart strap calls when the disk starts, and it transfers control to one other routine. No pseudo-code was produced, so nothing beyond that is known.

name: load_boot_address_then_call
description: Seven-instruction boot block routine that is referenced by an address load, reached from two callers, and calls one other routine. No pseudo-code was produced, so only its call pattern is known.

name: forward_boot_entry_call
description: Single-instruction boot block entry that the Kickstart strap calls when the disk starts, and it transfers control to one other routine. No pseudo-code was produced, so nothing beyond that is known.

name: load_boot_address_then_call
description: Seven-instruction boot block routine that is referenced by an address load, reached from two callers, and calls one other routine. No pseudo-code was produced, so only its call pattern is known.

name: load_copper_list_and_jump
description: Writes a pointer into the copper list location register and then strobes the copper jump register, which starts a copper program. It also calls one other routine and is referenced by an absolute address.

name: set_copper_list_pointer
description: Stores an address register value into the first copper list location register, which points the copper at a new display list. It makes no calls and returns directly.

name: set_interrupt_and_dma_state
description: Writes the interrupt enable, DMA enable, interrupt request and disk control registers, and reads the CIA port registers that carry the fire buttons and disk status. It calls four other routines and a return-from-exception routine, and it is entered from a move-quick-and-return routine.

name: forward_two_routine_calls
description: Three-instruction routine that is referenced by an address load, reached from two callers, and calls two other routines. No pseudo-code was produced, so its behaviour is limited to that call structure.

name: spin_forever_idle_loop
description: Four-instruction routine whose only body is an endless loop, so it never returns to its callers once entered. It is reached from three callers.

name: decode_bitplane_draw_commands
description: Reads command bytes from a stream and dispatches on each through a large switch, including a case that writes a bit-masked pattern into five bitplane-style regions spaced one row of 40 bytes apart. Other cases set shared state and call through a dispatch table, and the routine returns once it reaches an end code.

name: dispatch_draw_command_bytes
description: Starts a command-byte dispatcher with the same case structure as its neighbour, including a bit-masked write into five plane-style regions, and makes one call through a dispatch table. It returns the data register pair when the stream ends.

name: return_immediately_stub
description: Single-instruction routine that only returns to its caller and does no other work. It is referenced by address from one caller and calls an empty routine.

name: return_immediately_stub
description: Single-instruction routine that only returns to its caller and does no other work. It is not reached from a recorded caller, and it calls an empty routine.

name: copy_row_bytes_into_planes
description: Loops over eight rows at a stride of 40 bytes, copying each source byte into four plane regions and then clearing the destination bits that the data register's low bits do not select. It is referenced by address from one caller.

name: clear_and_set_plane_bits
description: Loops over eight rows at a stride of 40 bytes, clearing one bit position in five plane regions and then setting it from the source byte where the matching mask bit is on. It is reached from an unreached gap in the code.

name: copy_row_bytes_masked
description: Loops over eight rows at a stride of 40 bytes, writing each source byte into four plane regions and then clearing the bits that the mask in the data register does not select. It is referenced by address from one caller.

name: blend_source_bits_into_planes
description: Loops over eight rows at a stride of 40 bytes, clearing a bit position in five plane regions and then setting it from the source byte where the matching mask bit is on. It is reached from an unreached gap and has one caller.

name: init_state_wait_for_zero
description: Stores two starting values into shared state words, then calls a routine in a loop and repeats until the word it returns is zero. It is entered from three callers and calls three other routines.

name: init_alt_wait_for_zero
description: Stores a different pair of starting values into the shared state words than its neighbour, then calls a routine in a loop until the returned word reaches zero. It is entered from three callers.

name: clear_colour_register_block
description: Writes zero into a block of 32 consecutive colour registers, four per iteration over eight iterations, starting at the first colour register. It makes no calls and returns.

name: scale_colors_into_palette
description: Writes 30 colour entries from a table into the palette registers, scaling each red, green and blue nibble by a shared brightness value with rounding. It then steps the brightness value up or down and advances a step counter.

name: save_registers_and_copy_trampoline
description: Waits until a status byte clears, copies a block of code words into a RAM area, then writes the current data and address register values into a save area after it. It records a pointer to that save area and finishes by setting the status byte to a non-zero value.

name: raise_trap_and_set_status
description: Raises the trap exception with vector number one and then sets a status byte to all ones. It is referenced from one caller and calls one other routine.

name: store_d7_and_set_status
description: Stores the seventh data register into a shared global and then sets a status byte to all ones. It makes no calls and is referenced by address from one caller.

name: copy_block_and_count_bytes
description: Copies a block of words from a source pointer into a destination buffer, with the count taken from the sixth data register. It then scans forward for a marker word and stores the number of bytes skipped in a shared counter.

name: store_low_word_global
description: Stores the low word of the data register into a shared global variable and returns. It makes no calls and is referenced by address from one caller.

name: halt_in_endless_loop
description: Does nothing except loop forever, so it never returns once entered. It is referenced by address from one caller and calls one other routine.

name: load_timer_and_wait
description: When a status byte is zero, loads a fixed timing value into a shared global and then loops until a second status byte becomes non-zero. Otherwise it returns immediately, and it calls one other routine.

name: start_idle_pending_slot
description: Checks a shared enable value and, when a pending slot is idle, calls one routine, marks the slot busy by setting its high byte, and clears a companion flag. Otherwise it returns without action.

name: arm_pending_slot_when_idle
description: When a status word is zero, calls one routine, sets the high byte of the word to ones, and clears a companion flag. It returns without action when the word is already set.

name: arm_cia_timer_countdown
description: When a pending word is set and its companion flag is clear, configures a CIA control register, loads a 16-bit count into the timer registers and sets the interrupt control value. Otherwise it clears the pending word and returns.

name: arm_cia_timer_when_idle
description: Performs the same timer-arming step as its neighbour with the early return removed, so it arms the timer whenever its companion flag is clear. Otherwise it clears the pending word.

name: clear_pending_slot_state
description: Stores a pointer and then zero into a shared pending slot, clearing its pending state. It makes no calls and returns directly.

name: program_cia_timer_count
description: Sets the run-mode bits of a CIA control register, writes the interrupt control value, and loads a 16-bit count from the data register into the timer low and high registers. It is entered from three callers.

name: call_if_flag_set
description: Calls one routine only when a shared flag byte is non-zero, and returns otherwise. It has no other work.

name: forward_call_then_return
description: Calls one other routine and then returns, adding no other work. It is referenced by address from one caller.

name: handle_cia_a_interrupt_status
description: Reads the CIA-A interrupt control and port registers, and when a specific status bit is set it updates a port control bit, computes a byte from another CIA-A port into a lookup location, and reprograms the interrupt control register. It also writes the interrupt request register.

name: dispatch_cia_b_pending_bits
description: Reads a pending-bit byte from the CIA-B interrupt control register, clears the bits it handles, and calls one routine when the lowest bit is set and another when bit three is set. It writes a ones value to a flag byte when bit two is set.

name: service_pending_bit_tail
description: Checks two pending bits, sets a flag byte when the second is set, clears the handled bits, and calls one routine when the third bit is set. It is the tail of its neighbour and reads the CIA-B port register.

name: advance_button_poll_counter
description: Masks a state byte, calls one routine, saves the result into a shared slot, and advances a poll counter. It also increments a second counter and resets it when the state byte is zero; the facts show reads of the interrupt request registers and the potentiometer port that carries the right and middle buttons.

name: reset_port_bytes_state
description: Zeroes four byte-wide hardware registers at fixed addresses, sets a shared state value and clears a counter. It returns the data register combined with a constant.

name: enter_port_reset_sequence
description: Single-instruction entry into the port reset sequence, which zeroes four byte-wide hardware registers and sets a shared state value. It is referenced by address from five callers.

name: reset_port_bytes_long_entry
description: Longer entry point into the port reset routine, recorded at 129 instructions, where only the opening part is visible in the decompiled output. That part zeroes four byte-wide hardware registers and sets a shared state value before returning.

name: reset_port_state_and_read
description: Opens by zeroing four byte-wide hardware registers and setting a shared state value, and the facts also show a read of the CIA-B port register and one call. The decompiled body is shared with its neighbours, so the remaining detail is limited.

name: cycle_indexed_port_bytes
description: Sets the top bit of one hardware byte, clears another, and writes two bytes taken from a table at a rotating index into two more hardware bytes. It cycles the index through three values and calls a routine from a dispatch table when a flag is clear.

name: advance_port_index_and_call
description: Returns when a flag byte is zero; otherwise it increments a shared index byte and calls one routine, setting the byte to a fixed value on one branch. It is referenced by address from two callers.

name: init_audio_channels_and_table
description: Builds a table of pointers from a block of byte values, then clears the four audio channel volume registers and sets a state word that marks the setup as active. It calls three other routines and a no-op routine.

name: silence_audio_channels
description: Writes zero to all four audio channel volume registers and resets a shared audio state byte to zero. It makes no calls and returns directly.

name: step_index_when_enabled
description: Returns when a flag byte is zero; otherwise it steps a shared index byte and calls one routine. It has the same index step as its neighbour and is referenced by address from one caller.

name: reset_index_and_call
description: Sets a shared index byte to zero, increments it, and calls one routine. The later branch can never run because its comparison is always true, so the routine always takes the zero-reset path.

name: set_status_and_call
description: Sets a shared status byte to all ones and calls one routine, then returns its stack value unchanged. It is referenced by address from one caller.

name: load_audio_channel_pointers
description: Masks a shared byte and calls a routine six times, then two more times when a flag is set, and the facts show it writes the four audio channel location registers. It returns no value.

name: set_dma_request_word
description: Stores a value with its top bit set into a shared word when a status nibble is not full or a companion flag is clear. The facts list the DMA control register, which uses that top bit as its enable convention.

name: load_sequence_entry_record
description: Loads a four-byte entry from an input block into a record and, when the entry's high nibble is non-zero, copies a parameter row into the record's pointer, count and step fields. It then returns a computed value, or calls another routine when the entry is not yet active.

name: copy_sequence_entry_fields
description: Sets a record's address field from a supplied offset and copies its values into an output buffer when the entry is active, returning the stored value. Otherwise it calls one routine.

name: copy_record_to_buffer

name: compare_value_with_limit
description: Masks a record's value to twelve bits, stores it in the record and clears a flag. It sets the flag to all ones when the value is below the stored limit.

name: clear_record_pending_word
description: Zeroes a 16-bit pending field in a record and returns. It makes no calls.

name: decode_effect_command_nibble

name: set_flag_bit_from_parameter

name: set_status_all_ones

name: store_param_then_set_status

name: clamp_parameter_to_limit

name: store_low_bits_as_mode

name: write_audio_channel_values

name: clamp_and_store_record_field

name: apply_effect_command_value

name: lookup_threshold_table_entry

name: lookup_threshold_table_low_nibble

name: lookup_threshold_table_by_column

name: subtract_param_clamp_floor

name: call_constant_loader_routine

name: init_text_entries_from_string

name: run_two_blitter_passes

description: Single-instruction routine that only returns to its caller and does no other work. It is entered from outside the static flow.

name: call_handler_then_store_flags
description: Calls a handler through a pointer in an object, sets a shared word to all high values three times, then compares a shared counter with a fixed value and calls a handler from the object in either branch. It finishes by writing a byte built from comparison flags to a pointer.

name: store_long_bytes_bcd_add
description: Stores the four bytes of a 32-bit value into consecutive memory locations, then performs a decimal-coded addition with carry handling. It calls routines twice and sets a shared flag when a value is non-zero.

name: forward_single_routine_call
description: Nine-instruction routine reached from an unreached gap that calls one other routine. No pseudo-code was produced, so nothing beyond that call is known.

name: call_through_dispatch_slot
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer read from a dispatch slot at a fixed offset in a shared block, then returns. It is entered from three callers.

name: call_dispatch_slot_return_regs
description: Calls a routine through a dispatch slot at a fixed offset in a shared block, then returns the data register pair unchanged. It is entered from one caller.

name: clear_shared_word_value
description: Stores zero into a shared word and returns. It makes no calls and is reached from an unreached gap.

name: call_slot_branch_on_result
description: Calls a routine through a dispatch slot and, when it returns non-zero, calls a second dispatch slot. The facts also show a reference to a text string that names a script file.

name: forward_single_routine_call
description: Calls one other routine and returns the data register pair unchanged. It is reached from an unreached gap.

name: update_button_state_bit
description: When the potentiometer port bit that carries the right and middle buttons is low and the matching state bit is clear, sets the state bit; when the port bit is high, clears it. It calls two routines.

name: set_bit_in_state_byte
description: Sets one bit, chosen by the low three bits of a data register, in a state byte. It returns immediately afterwards.

name: clear_bit_in_state_byte
description: Clears one bit, chosen by the low three bits of a data register, in a state byte. It returns immediately afterwards.

name: copy_field_wait_status_bit
description: Copies a value from an input record into a field at a fixed offset, then polls a shared status byte until its bit six clears. The facts also show reads of the CIA-A port and the DMA control read register.

name: copy_words_and_set_control
description: Copies 20 words from a source table into a fixed RAM area, then sets a control bit mask, writes its inverse to a CIA-B port, and polls a status bit for a bounded count. It calls several routines.

name: decompress_bit_stream_block
description: Decodes a compressed block by reading bits from a stream, either copying a run of earlier output bytes or assembling a literal byte from several bits, and writes the output backwards into a buffer. It returns a computed value once the output reaches its start point.

name: shift_bit_buffer_right
description: Shifts a 32-bit bit buffer right by a count from a data register, loading a new word from memory with a leading one bit whenever the buffer runs empty. It makes no calls of its own.

name: set_port_select_and_wait
description: Converts a shared value into a single-bit select mask, writes its inverse to a CIA-B port, and polls a status bit for a bounded count before returning.

name: pulse_control_port_bits
description: Writes six byte values to a control port in sequence, clearing one of four bits in turn between full restores. It takes no data input and is a fixed pulse sequence.

name: wait_until_status_bit_clears
description: Repeatedly calls one routine while a status bit in a hardware register at a fixed offset is set, then clears a shared byte and returns.

name: step_value_with_port_pulses
description: Moves a shared value toward a target one step at a time, writing alternating control bytes to a port with a fixed delay between steps. It calls a routine first when the value is negative.

name: pulse_control_port_repeat
description: Repeats a count of writes to a control port, alternating between two values with a fixed delay after each pair. It makes no calls.

name: run_nested_port_loop
description: Runs nested loops over a counter, setting a shared counter to eight and decrementing it while calling routines on each step, and then calls one more routine. It is entered from one caller.

name: setup_disk_read_registers
description: Writes disk pointer, length and sync registers and a disk control word into a record, with the sync value matching the standard MFM sync pattern. It then polls a status bit for a bounded count before rewriting the length. It is referenced from three callers.

name: verify_byte_then_compare_pair
description: Calls a routine to get a byte and compares it with a value derived from a shared byte. When they match, it calls two routines, compares their results, and calls a third routine when they agree.

name: merge_masked_longword_bits
description: Combines two 32-bit values using a mask in a data register, taking masked bits from the second value and the masked first value doubled, and returns the result.

name: merge_masked_block_longwords
description: Applies the same masked merge to each longword of a block and writes the results to a destination buffer. The block length comes from a word count in a data register.

name: xor_block_masked_checksum
description: XORs a block of longwords together starting from the first one, then returns the result masked by a value in a data register. The block length comes from a word in a data register.

name: process_block_entry
description: Ninety-one instruction routine that is referenced by an absolute move and called from two places. No pseudo-code was produced, so only its size and callers are known.

name: forward_jump_vector_entry
description: Nineteen-instruction routine, reached from a reference run, that calls a jump-table entry which passes control on to a fixed address. No pseudo-code was produced, so only that call is known.

name: forward_single_routine_call
description: Two-instruction routine whose only decompiler output is a stack pointer note and a list of removed unreachable blocks, so its behaviour beyond one call is not recoverable.

name: initialise_display_and_hardware
description: Very large routine of 775 instructions that touches the copper, display, interrupt, DMA, CIA and colour registers and calls 37 other routines. Its visible decompiled output is only a list of removed unreachable blocks, so detail is limited to those registers and calls.

name: copy_table_rows_into_planes
description: Calls one routine eleven times, then copies rows of words from a source table, selecting each row by a four-bit index from a list and writing interleaved words into a buffer with fixed strides.

name: clear_buffer_and_copy_rows
description: Zeroes 8000 longwords of a buffer, calls one routine ten times, then copies rows of words from a source table into the buffer, selecting each row by a four-bit index from a list.

name: run_three_setup_routines
description: Calls three other routines and is referenced by an absolute move. No pseudo-code was produced, so only those calls are known.

name: clear_active_slot_blocks
description: Walks a table of 30 entries and, for each active entry, clears longwords at regular intervals across a block at an offset from a shared base. The table entries are 18 words apart.

name: clear_strided_record_block
description: Clears a strided run of records starting at a shared base offset, writing a longword and a word of zeros into each record, with the count taken from a shared value.

name: blit_active_table_entries
description: Walks 30 table entries and, for each active one, programs the blitter registers from its position and pointer fields and then calls a routine to start the blit. It resets the blitter mask registers at the end.

name: shift_and_merge_plane_rows
description: Rotates groups of five source words by a shift amount from a shared value, then merges them into four bitplane regions using masks, repeating for a row count held in a shared word. The output advances by a fixed row stride on each pass.

name: clear_two_bitplane_buffers
description: Zeroes two blocks of 8000 longwords each, writing both blocks in lockstep. It makes no calls.

name: copy_words_into_two_planes
description: Copies a source block of words into two bitplane buffers in lockstep, writing four words per step, twenty steps per row, for 200 rows, and advancing both destinations by a row stride.

name: select_bitplane_buffer_address
description: Assigns one of two bitplane buffer addresses into a shared word and then inverts that word. The conditional branch makes the final value hard to read, so its exact effect is uncertain.

name: clear_sixteen_words
description: Zeroes sixteen consecutive words starting at a shared location. It makes no calls.

name: copy_sixteen_words_from_source
description: Copies sixteen words from a source pointer into consecutive words of a shared location. It makes no calls.

name: handle_keyboard_serial_flag
description: When a status bit is set, clears a status byte and calls one routine, then sets the status byte to a fixed value. The facts link it to the keyboard serial data register and the interrupt request register.

name: decode_joystick_direction_bits
description: Derives direction bits from the joystick and mouse movement registers using exclusive-or logic, then stores them with fire-button bits in a shared byte. It decodes twice and clears the shared word at the end.

name: decode_packed_stream_block
description: Decodes a packed block by reading bits through a bit-reader routine, either copying a run of earlier output bytes or assembling literal bytes, and writes the output backwards into a buffer. It calls two bit-reader routines and two others, and returns zero or minus one depending on whether output ended at the start point.

name: decode_packed_literal_tail
description: Decoder fragment that reads eight bits into a literal byte and writes it backwards, then falls into run-copy logic. It is reached from an unreached gap and calls one other routine.

name: copy_packed_runs_backward
description: Decoder fragment that copies runs of earlier output bytes backwards into the buffer, then decides whether to read another literal or a new run. It calls a bit-reader routine and two others.

name: decode_packed_run_loop
description: Decoder fragment that copies runs of earlier output bytes backwards and chooses between literal bytes and runs from the bit stream. It calls a bit-reader routine and two others, and is entered from two callers.

name: return_minus_one
description: Returns minus one immediately and makes no calls. It is reached from an unreached gap.

name: allocate_free_slot_from_table
description: Counts down a shared counter and, when it reaches zero, scans 30 entries for an idle slot and fills the first idle one from a source table with position and timing fields. The facts also show a read of the vertical beam position register.

name: update_active_slot_timers
description: Walks 30 slot entries and, for each active one, advances its position by a type-dependent step and deactivates it once it passes a fixed limit. It also counts down a per-slot timer that toggles a flag when it expires.

name: copy_shifted_rows_clear_buffer
description: Clears a buffer, then copies rows of packed source words into it shifted by an amount held in a shared counter, interleaving the results and clearing padding words between rows. The decompiled output is truncated, so later steps are not recovered.

name: clear_then_copy_shifted_rows
description: Zeroes a block of buffer words, then copies shifted rows of packed source words into it with padding cleared between rows. The decompiled output is truncated, so later steps are not recovered.

name: copy_shifted_rows_second_source
description: Clears a buffer, then copies shifted rows from a second source table into it, four words per group, with the shift amount taken from a shared counter. The decompiled output is truncated, so later steps are not recovered.

name: copy_shifted_rows_third_source
description: Clears a buffer, then copies shifted rows from a third source table into it, four words per group, with the shift amount taken from a shared counter. The decompiled output is truncated, so later steps are not recovered.

name: draw_text_glyphs_from_string
description: Draws a text string by reading character bytes until an end marker, moving down a line on a line-break marker, and otherwise copying an eight-row glyph from a font table into the plane buffer. Each glyph is selected by subtracting a fixed base from the character code.
